summary: Voters approve a street bond and the city starts with repaving, leaving the costly rebuilds for later years.
realLife: Dallas voters approved about $534 million in 2017 for roughly 1,000 street and alley projects, planning 567 lane miles of resurfacing and 82 lane miles of reconstruction. A year later, 142 projects were complete and 30 underway, and city staff said resurfacing came first because reconstruction costs more and takes longer to plan; potholes were paid for from general funds.
